text:
Happy Halloween! We're starting out clear and chilly, around 40 and feeling colder, so grab a real jacket. Today stays mostly sunny with a high near 47, and some high clouds drift in from mid-afternoon into the evening. High pressure is sitting right on top of us, so the wind stays light.

For trick-or-treating, plan on low to mid 40s early, then temperatures slide into the 30s after the sun sets around 5:45. Put a warm layer under the costume and send the kids out with hats and gloves. Tonight bottoms out around 30 under mostly clear skies.

Sunday is the nicer day: sunny, a light south breeze, and a high near 57. The clocks go back an hour at 2 AM, so turn them back before bed tonight. Next week stays mild, with highs climbing toward 60 and a bit beyond, and the next real shot at rain holds off until late in the week. That one could be a wet system, though the timing is still unsettled.

AFD WHAT CHANGED (same regional caveat): As of 225 AM EDT Saturday... The forecast is in good shape. No major changes needed.
AFD DISCUSSION (the forecaster's full reasoning, same regional caveat; their temps are area-wide ranges):
KEY MESSAGE 1: Surface high pressure will build into northern New York and Vermont throughout the day. It will be a chilly day to wrap up the month of October with temperatures lingering in the 40s for most locations. Mountain clouds may briefly scatter out, but an upper vort will quickly dive southeast and produce some additional mid to high clouds mid-afternoon into the evening hours. Main concern for today will be continued low humidity across the region. Eastern slopes of the Adirondacks into south-central Vermont will likely observe minimum relative humidities from 30-40%. Areas north will likely see values in the 40-50% range. Modest mixing, but overall light flow should keep sustained winds around 5-10 mph with a few gusts around 15-18 mph during the afternoon. High pressure will be overhead, and so efficient radiational cooling is expected. Trick-or-treaters can expect a chilly experience, but at least it will not be the wet and windy weather of last year. Temperatures will quickly fall into the 30s after sunset, and overnight lows will reach into the 20s for most. During the pre-dawn hours, southwesterly flow will become reestablished as high pressure moves offshore. Moderating conditions will bring temperatures up into the mid 50s to near 60 by Sunday afternoon. Initially low dewpoints will begin to rise, and relative humidity will become less of a concern. Minimum relative humidity values on Sunday will likely be at or above 40% outside a few localized areas in the Upper Valley. KEY MESSAGE 2: Scanning through the early part of next week, guidance continues to trend away from a cold frontal passage Monday night into Tuesday. This means warm advection is slated to begin a bit sooner. Temperatures will warm into the upper 50s to mid 60s during the afternoon, with clouds north. A mid to upper level ridge tilted northwest to southeast should let some moisture crest over its axis over the eastern Great Lakes region. It's possible some rain will be within our side of the international border. Amounts, if any, will be light. Even without the rain, there will be greater sky cover. This will limit heating a bit for Tuesday, but it will still likely climb into the upper 50s to mid 60s during the afternoon. KEY MESSAGE 3: Models continue to depict a full meridional trough to approach late next week. Consensus is moderately strong that ridging will slowly slide eastward Tuesday into Wednesday as a large area of low pressure is favored to develop over the Plains while jet energy is projected to dip into the the southern states. The result could be a more mature type front and system passage sometime between Wednesday night and Friday night. Passage timing remains most suspect given the dependence on the movement speed of a large, semi- persistent ridge. However, the pressure gradient will likely be compounded across the Northeast Wednesday into Thursday supporting some southerly breezes and promoting gusts 20-30 mph, especially in channeled areas l

WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) - Happy Halloween! Today will be a bit chilly, unfortunately, but otherwise it looks good for trick-or-treating. The morning will be mostly sunny, then the afternoon will turn partly sunny before becoming mainly clear again for the evening. Highs will be in the mid to upper 40s. For trick-or-treat time, temperatures will be generally in the low to mid-40s depending on what time you head out. You’ll definitely want a jacket, but thankfully the wind will be light. Sunday will be mostly sunny and warmer with highs in the 50s. The fire risk will remain elevated, but it has been reduced a bit due to the light showers from Thursday night. A reminder that we’re back to Standard Time Sunday at 2 AM. Remember to turn your clocks back 1 hour before bedtime Saturday night. The first week of November will feature some pretty nice temperatures. Monday will be partly sunny with pleasant highs in the mid-50s to low 60s. Lows will be relatively mild in the 40s. Election Day will be mostly cloudy but otherwise pleasant with highs back in the mid-50s to low 60s. A few spots could reach the mid-60s on Wednesday. The next chance for showers will be Thursday. This could be one of the wetter days we’ve had in quite some time, but models differ with the placement of the storm system. Friday will have a return to dry conditions with cooler but seasonable highs in the mid-50s.
NBC5 METEOROLOGIST (2026-10-30T21:51:00Z — same caveat): Plenty of sun this weekend, chilly for trick-or-treaters — Tonight gets cold as skies gradually clear, with lows in the 20s and 30s. Halloween weekend starts bright but cool on Saturday, with highs in the upper 40s. Sunday turns a bit milder, with highs in the mid-50s, as sun mixes with late day clouds. Most of next week looks mild for early November, with highs pushing past 60 several days in a row. We'll have more clouds overall, and a greater chance for substantial rain to arrive by late week.
